reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Mr. Johnson asked the students in his school about their favorite subject.

This pie chart shows how many students liked each of 5 subjects.

[Image: Pie chart titled Favorite Subject, divided into various sizes and labeled with Math about one-third, Science about one-fourth, History about one-fifth, Gym less than one-fifth, and Music less than one-eighth.]

Which graph shows the same information as the pie chart?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: Bar graph with y-axis labeled number of students and values from 0 to 25; x-axis with 5 columns, Math value of 30, Science value of 25, History value of 20, Gym value of 17, Music value of 8.]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: Bar graph with y-axis labeled number of students and values from 0 to 25; x-axis with 5 columns, Math value of 30, Science value of 15, History value of 15, Gym value of 15, Music value of 14.]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: Bar graph with y-axis labeled number of students and values from 0 to 25; x-axis with 5 columns, Math value of 20, Science value of 25, History value of 30, Gym value of 17, Music value of 8.]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: Bar graph with y-axis labeled number of students and values from 0 to 25; x-axis with 5 columns, Math value of 25, Science value of 30, History value of 20, Gym value of 8, Music value of 12.]

reference_items.figure_description:
A pie chart titled "Favorite Subject" is divided into five sectors: Math (the largest sector, about one-third of the circle), Science (the second largest, about one-fourth of the circle), History (about one-fifth of the circle), Gym (smaller than History), and Music (the smallest sector, less than one-eighth of the circle). In order of sector size from largest to smallest: Math, Science, History, Gym, Music.

Each of the four response options shows a vertical bar graph with the vertical axis labeled "Number of Students" ranging from 0 to 35 with grid lines every 5 units, and the horizontal axis showing five subjects: Math, Science, History, Gym, Music.
- Graph A: Math = 30, Science = 25, History = 20, Gym = 17, Music = 8.
- Graph B: Math = 30, Science = 15, History = 15, Gym = 15, Music = 14.
- Graph C: Math = 20, Science = 25, History = 30, Gym = 17, Music = 8.
- Graph D: Math = 25, Science = 30, History = 20, Gym = 8, Music = 16.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
